answers.solution:
Let the number be \(x\).

Correct answer = \(x \times \frac{5}{6} = \frac{5x}{6}\)

Shyam's answer = \(x \div \frac{5}{6} = \frac{6x}{5}\)

Difference: \(\frac{6x}{5} - \frac{5x}{6} = 55\)

\(\frac{36x - 25x}{30} = 55\), so \(\frac{11x}{30} = 55\)

\(x = \frac{55 \times 30}{11} = 150\)

Check: \(\frac{6}{5} \times 150 = 180\), \(\frac{5}{6} \times 150 = 125\), and \(180 - 125 = 55\).

So, the given number is 150.

answers.label: Q.2
answers.solution:
A number divisible by each of 16, 36, 45, 48 is a multiple of their LCM.

\(16 = 2^4\), \(36 = 2^2 \times 3^2\), \(45 = 3^2 \times 5\), \(48 = 2^4 \times 3\)

LCM = \(2^4 \times 3^2 \times 5 = 720\)

The greatest four-digit number is 9999. Dividing: \(9999 = 720 \times 13 + 639\).

Required number = \(9999 - 639 = 9360\) \((= 720 \times 13)\).

So, the highest four-digit number is 9360.

Use \(\frac{M_1 D_1}{W_1} = \frac{M_2 D_2}{W_2}\).

\(\frac{12 \times 16}{10} = \frac{8 \times D_2}{20}\)

\(D_2 = \frac{12 \times 16 \times 20}{10 \times 8} = \frac{3840}{80} = 48\)

(Check: 10 rooms need \(12 \times 16 = 192\) person-days, so 20 rooms need 384 person-days; 8 people take \(\frac{384}{8} = 48\) days.)

So, 8 people can paint 20 rooms in 48 days.

The angles of a quadrilateral add up to \(360^\circ\).

Let the angles be \(3k, 5k, 7k, 9k\).

\(3k + 5k + 7k + 9k = 360^\circ\), so \(24k = 360^\circ\) and \(k = 15^\circ\).

Angles: \(3 \times 15 = 45^\circ\), \(5 \times 15 = 75^\circ\), \(7 \times 15 = 105^\circ\), \(9 \times 15 = 135^\circ\).

Check: \(45 + 75 + 105 + 135 = 360^\circ\).

So, the angles are \(45^\circ, 75^\circ, 105^\circ, 135^\circ\).

\(\frac{25}{9} = \left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^2\), so \(\left(\frac{25}{9}\right)^{-\frac{11}{2}} = \left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{2 \times \left(-\frac{11}{2}\right)} = \left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{-11}\)

Left side = \(\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{-5} \times \left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{-11} = \left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{-16}\)

So \(\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{-16} = \left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{8x}\)

Equating powers: \(8x = -16\), so \(x = -2\).

So, \(x = -2\).

The number + 17 must be the smallest common multiple of 520 and 468, that is, their LCM.

\(520 = 2^3 \times 5 \times 13\)

\(468 = 2^2 \times 3^2 \times 13\)

LCM = \(2^3 \times 3^2 \times 5 \times 13 = 8 \times 9 \times 65 = 4680\)

Required number = \(4680 - 17 = 4663\).

So, the smallest number is 4663.

answers.solution:
Driving time = \(\frac{500}{50} = 10\) hours.

The car stops after 100 km, 200 km, 300 km and 400 km. After 500 km the journey is over, so there is no stop then. Number of stops = 4.

Stopping time = \(4 \times \frac{1}{2} = 2\) hours.

Total time = \(10 + 2 = 12\) hours.

So, the car takes 12 hours.

answers.solution:
Let the speeds be \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) (m/s).

A train passes a standing man in the time it takes to cover its own length:

Length of first train = \(27 v_1\); length of second train = \(17 v_2\).

Crossing each other (opposite directions), they cover the sum of their lengths at relative speed \(v_1 + v_2\):

\(\frac{27 v_1 + 17 v_2}{v_1 + v_2} = 23\)

\(27 v_1 + 17 v_2 = 23 v_1 + 23 v_2\)

\(4 v_1 = 6 v_2\), so \(\frac{v_1}{v_2} = \frac{6}{4} = \frac{3}{2}\)

So, the ratio of their speeds is 3 : 2.

answers.solution:
Let length, breadth, height be \(4k, 3k, 2k\).

Volume: \(4k \times 3k \times 2k = 24k^3 = 5184\)

\(k^3 = \frac{5184}{24} = 216\), so \(k = 6\).

Length = \(4 \times 6 = 24\) cm, breadth = \(3 \times 6 = 18\) cm, height = \(2 \times 6 = 12\) cm.

Check: 24, 18 and 12 are all multiples of 3 and of 2, so the cuboid can be cut exactly into 3 cm cubes or 2 cm cubes; and \(24 \times 18 \times 12 = 5184\).

So, the cuboid is 24 cm long, 18 cm broad and 12 cm high.

answers.label: Q.12
answers.solution:
The three lines are parallel. Let V be the vertex where the two slanting lines meet on the middle line, and extend the middle line to the right of V.

The reflex angle \(235^\circ\) at V is split by this extension into an upper part and a lower part.

Upper part: the angle \(2x\) at the top line and the upper part at V are co-interior angles (same side of the slanting line, between parallel lines), so the upper part = \(180^\circ - 2x\).

Lower part: the angle \(3x + 5^\circ\) at the bottom line and the lower part at V are alternate angles, so the lower part = \(3x + 5^\circ\).

So \((180^\circ - 2x) + (3x + 5^\circ) = 235^\circ\)

\(185^\circ + x = 235^\circ\), so \(x = 50^\circ\).

(Equivalently, the angle at V on the left side is \(360^\circ - 235^\circ = 125^\circ = 2x + (180^\circ - (3x + 5^\circ))\), which also gives \(x = 50^\circ\).) The figure is not drawn to scale: with \(x = 50^\circ\), the angle marked \(2x\) is \(100^\circ\).

So, \(x = 50^\circ\).

answers.solution:
The "?" printed after the bar term is a stray mark; it is ignored. The bar (vinculum) over \(9 - 5x\) means it is worked out first, like a bracket.

Step 1 (bar): \(8 - (9 - 5x) = 8 - 9 + 5x = 5x - 1\)

Step 2 (small bracket): \(3(5x - 1) = 15x - 3\)

Step 3 (curly bracket): \(-17x + 15x - 3 = -2x - 3\)

Step 4: \(-4\{-2x - 3\} = 8x + 12\)

Step 5 (square bracket): \(-11x + 8x + 12 = -3x + 12\)

Step 6: \(-7[-3x + 12] = 21x - 84\)

Step 7: \(84 + 21x - 84 = 21x\)

So, the expression simplifies to \(21x\).

The rectangle ABCD is inside the circle with all four corners on it, so its diagonal is a diameter.

Diagonal AC = \(\sqrt{8^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{64 + 36} = \sqrt{100} = 10\) cm, so radius = 5 cm.

Area of circle = \(3.14 \times 5 \times 5 = 78.5\ \text{cm}^2\).

Area of rectangle = \(8 \times 6 = 48\ \text{cm}^2\).

Shaded area = \(78.5 - 48 = 30.5\ \text{cm}^2\).

So, the area of the shaded region is \(30.5\ \text{cm}^2\).

SP of 90 pens = Rs 160 at 20% loss, so SP = 80% of CP.

CP of 90 pens = \(160 \times \frac{100}{80} = 200\) rupees.

CP of 1 pen = \(\frac{200}{90} = \frac{20}{9}\) rupees.

For 20% profit, SP of 1 pen = \(\frac{20}{9} \times \frac{120}{100} = \frac{8}{3}\) rupees.

Number of pens for Rs 96 = \(96 \div \frac{8}{3} = 96 \times \frac{3}{8} = 36\).

So, 36 ball pens should be sold for Rs 96.

Let the unit digit be \(y\); then the ten's digit is \(2y\).

Sum of digits: \(2y + y = 6\), so \(3y = 6\) and \(y = 2\).

Ten's digit = \(2 \times 2 = 4\).

Number = \(10 \times 4 + 2 = 42\).

So, the number is 42.

Let the can hold \(x\) bottles of oil.

At first it holds \(\frac{4}{5}x\) bottles.

6 bottles taken out and 4 poured in: net change = \(-6 + 4 = -2\) bottles.

\(\frac{4}{5}x - 2 = \frac{3}{4}x\)

\(\frac{4}{5}x - \frac{3}{4}x = 2\), so \(\frac{16x - 15x}{20} = 2\), \(\frac{x}{20} = 2\)

\(x = 40\)

Check: \(\frac{4}{5} \times 40 = 32\); \(32 - 6 + 4 = 30 = \frac{3}{4} \times 40\).

So, the can holds 40 bottles of oil.

answers.finalAnswer: Rs 5600 (at 7 1/2% for 2 years); Rs 2400 (at 8% for 3 years)
answers.solution:
Let Rs \(x\) be lent at \(7\frac{1}{2}\%\) for 2 years; the other part Rs \((8000 - x)\) at 8% for 3 years (simple interest).

Interest on first part = \(\frac{x \times 7.5 \times 2}{100} = \frac{15x}{100}\)

Interest on second part = \(\frac{(8000 - x) \times 8 \times 3}{100} = \frac{24(8000 - x)}{100}\)

Total: \(\frac{15x + 192000 - 24x}{100} = 1416\)

\(192000 - 9x = 141600\), so \(9x = 50400\) and \(x = 5600\).

Other part = \(8000 - 5600 = 2400\).

Check: \(5600 \times 0.15 = 840\), \(2400 \times 0.24 = 576\), \(840 + 576 = 1416\).

So, the two parts are Rs 5600 (at \(7\frac{1}{2}\%\)) and Rs 2400 (at 8%).

answers.solution:
The first term is printed with denominator 1, which is unusual and may be a misprint; the equation is solved as printed.

\(\frac{3x - 5}{1} - \frac{1 + x}{2} = 3 - \frac{x - 1}{4}\)

Multiply every term by 4 (LCM of 1, 2, 4):

\(4(3x - 5) - 2(1 + x) = 12 - (x - 1)\)

\(12x - 20 - 2 - 2x = 12 - x + 1\)

\(10x - 22 = 13 - x\)

\(11x = 35\)

\(x = \frac{35}{11} = 3\frac{2}{11}\)

Check: left side \(= \frac{105}{11} - 5 - \frac{46}{22} = \frac{50}{11} - \frac{23}{11} = \frac{27}{11}\); right side \(= 3 - \frac{24}{44} = 3 - \frac{6}{11} = \frac{27}{11}\).

(If the first denominator was meant to be 2, the same method gives \(x = 5\).)

So, \(x = \frac{35}{11}\).

Let the length of the train be \(L\) m and its speed \(v\) m/s.

Passing the man: \(L = 18v\).

Passing the platform: \(L + 330 = 40v\).

Subtract: \(330 = 22v\), so \(v = 15\) m/s.

Speed in km/h = \(15 \times \frac{18}{5} = 54\) km/h.

Length = \(18 \times 15 = 270\) m.

So, the speed of the train is 54 km/h and its length is 270 m.

answers.solution:
Let Priya's age at marriage be \(x\) years. Her present age is \(x + 8\).

\(x + 8 = 1\frac{2}{7} x = \frac{9}{7}x\)

\(\frac{9x}{7} - x = 8\), so \(\frac{2x}{7} = 8\) and \(x = 28\).

Present age of Priya = \(28 + 8 = 36\) years.

Daughter's present age = \(\frac{1}{6} \times 36 = 6\) years.

Daughter's age 3 years ago = \(6 - 3 = 3\) years.

So, her daughter was 3 years old 3 years ago.

answers.solution:
1 woman does \(\frac{1}{16 \times 12} = \frac{1}{192}\) of the work per day; 1 child does \(\frac{1}{24 \times 18} = \frac{1}{432}\).

Using 1728 (LCM of 192 and 432): a woman does \(\frac{9}{1728}\), a child \(\frac{4}{1728}\) per day.

17 women + 8 children per day: \(\frac{17 \times 9 + 8 \times 4}{1728} = \frac{153 + 32}{1728} = \frac{185}{1728}\)

Work in 8 days = \(\frac{1480}{1728}\); remaining = \(\frac{1728 - 1480}{1728} = \frac{248}{1728}\).

With 3 more children (11 children): \(\frac{153 + 44}{1728} = \frac{197}{1728}\) per day.

Time = \(\frac{248}{1728} \div \frac{197}{1728} = \frac{248}{197} \approx 1.26\) days.

The awkward answer suggests a misprint: if 12 women (not 17) start, the rate is \(\frac{140}{1728}\), 8 days do \(\frac{1120}{1728}\), the remaining \(\frac{608}{1728}\) at \(\frac{152}{1728}\) per day takes exactly 4 days.

So, as printed, they take \(\frac{248}{197}\) days (about 1.26 days) more.

Let the distance on foot be \(x\) km; distance by bicycle = \((61 - x)\) km.

Time on foot + time on bicycle = 9 hours:

\(\frac{x}{4} + \frac{61 - x}{9} = 9\)

Multiply by 36: \(9x + 4(61 - x) = 324\)

\(9x + 244 - 4x = 324\)

\(5x = 80\), so \(x = 16\).

Check: \(\frac{16}{4} = 4\) h and \(\frac{45}{9} = 5\) h, total 9 h.

So, he travelled 16 km on foot.

answers.solution:
Let the work last \(T\) days.

A works 2 days, B works \((T - 3)\) days, C works all \(T\) days.

One day's work: A = \(\frac{1}{10}\), B = \(\frac{1}{12}\), C = \(\frac{1}{15}\).

\(\frac{2}{10} + \frac{T - 3}{12} + \frac{T}{15} = 1\)

Multiply by 60: \(12 + 5(T - 3) + 4T = 60\)

\(12 + 5T - 15 + 4T = 60\)

\(9T = 63\), so \(T = 7\).

Check: A does \(\frac{2}{10}\), B does \(\frac{4}{12}\), C does \(\frac{7}{15}\); \(\frac{6 + 10 + 14}{30} = 1\).

So, the work lasted 7 days.
